review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of tubeDegree and pencilFiberEnergy. I searched the repo for other uses of pencilFiber. It is used only in this file; later files use pencil_fiber_regular_subset and pencilFiberEnergy. The proof of finite_planar_energy_regular_subset uses only local `let`s and `simp only`/`simp` calls with their own arguments, and I found no simp-loop or competing-rule problem there. The one finding is a missing simp-interface lemma for the new definition pencilFiber. I did not run Lean, so the proposed `mem_pencilFiber` lemma is untested.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def pencilFiber (P : Finset (Space 2))
    (T : Space 2 → Finset (Space 2)) (l : Space 2) : Finset (Space 2) :=
  P.filter fun x => l ∈ T x
findings.problem: The new definition `pencilFiber` has no membership characterisation lemma, so no canonical simp form for `x ∈ pencilFiber P T l`. The file already works around this by unfolding the definition by hand. In pencil_fiber_regular_subset, the final step uses `(Finset.mem_filter.mp (hSF hx)).2`, and the subset step uses `hSF.trans (Finset.filter_subset _ _)`. Both depend on the filter implementation. The other two lemmas, `pencilFiber_card` and `pencilFiber_energy`, are applied only through explicit `simpa only [...]` lists, and `pencilFiber_card` unfolds the definition inside `simp only [pencilFiber, ...]`. The definition therefore has no stable simp interface. Any later user has to unfold `pencilFiber` to a `filter`, which exposes the implementation.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] theorem mem_pencilFiber : x ∈ pencilFiber P T l ↔ x ∈ P ∧ l ∈ T x := by simp [pencilFiber]` and `theorem pencilFiber_subset : pencilFiber P T l ⊆ P := Finset.filter_subset _ _`. Then rewrite `fun x hx => (Finset.mem_filter.mp (hSF hx)).2` as `fun x hx => (mem_pencilFiber.mp (hSF hx)).2`, and use `pencilFiber_subset` in place of `Finset.filter_subset _ _`. Also consider tagging `pencilFiber_card` as `@[simp]`: its right-hand side `tubeDegree P T l` is the canonical normal form for the cardinality cast, and its left-hand side is not matched by any other rule. Keep `pencilFiber` itself non-reducible and not simp-unfolded.
findings.benefit: Proofs about pencil fibers can use `simp` instead of `Finset.mem_filter` and `Finset.filter_subset`. The `filter` implementation stays hidden. The rewriting `card ↦ tubeDegree` also becomes available automatically, which removes the explicit `simpa only [pencilFiber_card]` lists in pencil_fiber_regular_subset.
